subject: Food Science
title: Enzymatic Browning
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Enzymatic Browning.

hook.text: A sliced banana turns brown in minutes but a whole banana doesn't. Cutting releases the enzyme that starts browning.

buildup.text: Polyphenol oxidase meets phenolic compounds when cell walls break. Oxygen from air completes the reaction.

discovery.text: The brown pigment is melanin—the same family of pigments that colors human skin and hair.

twist.text: Lemon juice slows enzymatic browning because ascorbic acid is an antioxidant and the low pH inhibits the enzyme.

climax.text: Some browning is desired—tea processing deliberately crushes leaves to trigger enzymatic browning for flavor.

punchline.text: Cut, exposed, browned. The enzyme just needs oxygen and a chance.

quiz.question: Why does lemon juice prevent cut fruit from browning?
options: Its acid and antioxidant properties inhibit the browning enzyme
